# Batch L — section L-DISCRIM artifacts — MANIFEST

Worker: `opus5:lexec`. **Capture only.** No arm is classified and no outcome is called
correct. Every arm here exists because an earlier arm **could not FAIL** the claim it was
cited for, so each carries an explicit ability-to-fail control and writes `ARM-INVALID`
when that control does not hold.

## Lead with the table

**`TABLES.txt` is generated by `_harness/discrim-mktables.sh` from the arm artifacts.**
Every value in it is read out of an `ARM.txt` or `ledger.tsv`; nothing is typed by hand,
and it regenerates. It carries the ability-to-fail control per arm, the D1/D2 lineage
tuples read by exact key, the D3 per-gate reachability, the D4 disposition table, and the
D5 caught-alive results.

## Run-wide provenance

Frozen commit `72c729343a0117af2968b66e1c43f89ad25fc0b2`, frozen `ae` sha256
`b7b8aa9f…`; tool hashes in `_harness/env-record.txt`; `LANG=LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8`,
`TZ=UTC`; no live models, no network. Each arm in its own disposable sandbox under
`/tmp/aelx/L-DISCRIM/<arm>/`. The agent is a renamed copy of `bash` named `grok` running
`t100-fake.sh`, an unmodelled tool, so helper and nudge delivery are never gated by a
readiness sensor.

Instrumented copies used, measured from the tree: **D1 under L-HOOKS-v3, D5b under
L-HOOKS-v5, the other four on the unmodified frozen binary.** Each `ARM.txt` names its
`hook_patch_version` and the binary's own sha256.

## Common capture set (every arm)

`ARM.txt` (arm, roster ids, **`exists_because` — the claim the earlier arm could not
fail**, construction, patch version, binary sha256, the arm's own measured values) ·
`ledger.tsv`, written BY the checks as they run, one timestamped row per check ·
`<step>.stdout` / `.stderr` / `.rc` / `.invocation` · recursive `AE_HOME`, sessions and
archive manifests and a tmux snapshot at the named points · `preflight-tab.txt` (the
blocking environment-as-instrument proof, in the arm's own `env -i`) ·
`consumer-inproc.txt` + `tmux-argv.log` · `SHA256SUMS.txt`.

## Arms

### D1 — the parent tuple is RECORDED, not re-read

| field | value |
|---|---|
| exists because | the existing SC-824a arm deletes the parent archive at the barrier, so the launch has no tuple to record and the arm cannot show WHICH tuple a surviving child would carry |
| construction | a parent archive is built with `handover=2 pending=1` — non-zero and distinct; at the barrier after the launch parses its FIRST parent proof the controller REPLACES that archive, **at the same id**, with a second VALID archive carrying `handover=5 pending=3`; the launch is released and the child's recorded tuple is read BY EXACT KEY |
| ability to fail | **an ability-to-fail CONTROL runs first**: a `--from` against the REPLACEMENT alone, in its own throwaway `AE_HOME` clone, must record 5/3. If it does not, the replacement is simply unreadable and a measurement finding the first tuple would prove nothing — `ARM-INVALID`. Recorded in `control-child-tuple.txt` and `ledger.tsv` |
| artifacts | `parent-archive-meta.txt`, `parent-archive-digest.md`, `replacement.{meta,digest}.{before,after}` + `.diff` + `.mutation.txt`, `replacement.manifest.tsv`, `control-child-tuple.txt`, the per-barrier `*.controller.txt` and `*.parent-meta.swap.diff`, `child-tuple.txt` |

The replacement's counts are set **consistently in both `meta` and `digest.md`**, so the
tree stays internally consistent and the frozen validator still accepts it; the mutation
is mode-preserving and both byte diffs are recorded.

### D2 — counts survive a cycle

| field | value |
|---|---|
| exists because | every count in the existing lineage-durability arms is `0`, so losing the value and defaulting to zero produce the same reading |
| construction | the same `handover=2 pending=1` parent; a real `--from` child is launched, its tuple read, the child stopped and resumed, and its tuple read again BY EXACT KEY |
| ability to fail | the counts are asserted NON-ZERO **and distinct from each other** before the arm proceeds (`d_assert_counts_discriminating`); otherwise `ARM-INVALID`. A `0`, or a swap, would both be visible |
| artifacts | `tuple.1after-from.txt`, `tuple.2after-stop.txt`, `tuple.3after-resume.txt`, `tuple.across-cycle.diff` |

**Fixture note, recorded because the first attempt failed on it.** The non-zero counts are
producer-derived: `handover_count` from real `memo add --topic handover` calls,
`pending_request_count` from a real unanswered `ask`. The first fixture spawned a second
agent to receive the ask; `spawn` reported the brief undelivered, the spawned pane fell
back to a shell, `ask` then refused to send to it, and the pending count came out `0` —
which the ability-to-fail assertion caught as `ARM-INVALID` rather than letting a zero
through. The ask now targets the session's own live main agent.

### D3 — rsync recorder canary

| field | value |
|---|---|
| exists because | the SC-814 canary proved the ssh recorder and inherited an unproven rsync one: the valid-name transfer dies at the SSH probe and never reaches rsync |
| construction | the recorder is first exercised by a **DIRECT** rsync invocation through the same delegate-and-log shim; then ae's valid-name transfer path is run and **both gates that precede any rsync invocation** are captured verbatim in `gates.txt` |
| result | **`ARM-INVALID` as a canary — and that is the finding.** |

Measured: the recorder IS live (2 direct invocations recorded); ae's valid-name path
records **1 ssh invocation and 0 rsync invocations**, rc 1. Two independent gates precede
any rsync call and both fail on this host — the SSH probe (a plain `ssh <target>`, whose
config OpenSSH reads from the passwd-entry home, so a sandbox-only alias is unreachable;
the three routes to it are the operator's real `~/.ssh/config`, root for port 22, or an
argv-injecting ssh shim, the last **refused by standing ruling**), and
`rsync --protect-args --version`, which this host's only rsync (openrsync) does not
support, making the ae path unreachable for **any** target here. **Consequence, stated:
the SC-814 rsync zero remains a zero from an undemonstrated recorder on the ae path. No
zero is reported here as an observation.**

### D4 — SIGPIPE disposition, ability-to-fail control

| field | value |
|---|---|
| exists because | the existing SC-504b arm sets `SIG_DFL` in the child before exec, so its clean reading cannot be told apart from the harness having reset the disposition itself |
| construction | the SAME capture is run three times against three deliberately different dispositions handed to the producer — `SIG_DFL` reset by the harness, `SIG_IGN` **deliberately leaked** by the harness, and nothing set at all |
| ability to fail | the leaked `SIG_IGN` must be DETECTED — the `dfl` and `ign` exit codes must differ, else `ARM-INVALID`. Measured: `dfl` 141, `ign` 1, `inherit` 1 |
| artifacts | `sigpipe-harness.py` (byte copy of what ran), `sigpipe-record.{dfl,ign,inherit}.json`, `producer.*.stderr`, `producer.*.stdout.firstline`, `disposition-table.txt` (generated from the records) |

**Attribution limit, stated in `ARM.txt` and here.** The harness sets the disposition
before exec in the `dfl` and `ign` runs, so those runs report what the **harness** handed
the producer. They demonstrate the capture CAN fail; they cannot separate "ae leaked
nothing" from "the harness reset it first". Reading a live process's ignored-signal mask
is what would separate them, and macOS has no `/proc` equivalent for it, so this
construction cannot answer that question on this platform. That is the finding, not a
clean result.

### D5 — the supervisor caught alive, in two halves

| arm | method | caught alive | supervisor pid |
|---|---|---|---|
| `D5a-supervisor-real-timing` | a dedicated sampler process running `pgrep -f` with **no sleep**, started BEFORE the stop | YES | recorded in `ARM.txt` |
| `D5b-supervisor-held-at-entry` | the supervisor is **held at its own entry barrier** under L-HOOKS-v5 — no race to lose | YES | recorded in `ARM.txt` |

Both exist because the existing self-stop artifact is a post-hoc snapshot byte-identical
to `3post.ps.txt`, showing no supervisor at all while its `ARM.txt` asserts
`supervisor_observed=yes`. D5a answers whether an external sampler can catch it at real
timing and records the **achieved sampling rate** alongside the hit count; D5b removes the
race entirely and is where a deterministic lineage comes from. Each records the full argv
row, the live process table at that moment (`at-first-sight.ps.txt` / `at-barrier.ps.txt`)
and an ancestor walk taken **while the process was alive**
(`supervisor-lineage.txt`); D5b also diffs the live table against the post-hoc snapshot
(`ps.at-barrier-vs-post.diff`). `ARM-INVALID` if nothing is caught.

**Two superseded attempts are recorded rather than kept.** D5a's first version sampled
with a forked `ps -ax` pipeline at a 50 ms sleep and recorded ZERO sightings across 600
iterations while the same run's `stop-results.txt` showed the supervisor had done its
work — it measured the sampler, not the product; the `pgrep`-with-no-sleep loop catches
it. D5b's first version prefixed the in-pane command with `env -i`, which strips `$TMUX`
and `$TMUX_PANE`, so the identity route refused at C1 and no supervisor was ever spawned;
only the hook variables are added now, inline, leaving the pane environment intact. Both
are stated in the arms' own `ARM.txt`.

## Measured across the section

**6 arms. `ARM-INVALID`: 1 — D3, deliberately, and it carries the finding.** No arm
reports a clean result from a control it could not fail.

## Known limits of this section, stated

- D3's finding is about **this host**. A machine with rsync 3.0+ and a reachable ssh
  target would make the canary buildable; nothing here says what it would then show.
- D4 cannot attribute its clean case to ae on this platform, as stated above.
- D5a's hit count is a property of the sampler and the machine, not of the supervisor;
  the achieved rate is recorded alongside it so the two are never confused.
- The agent is an unmodelled fake, so nothing here exercises a TUI-modelled send path.
